newsitem.title: GERMANY: No progress seen in German coal subsidy talks.
newsitem.headline: No progress seen in German coal subsidy talks.

text.p: Talks between Chancellor Helmut Kohl and miners' leaders on the future of state aid to the German coal industry made no progress on Thursday, despite Kohl's offer to keep subsidy payments going until 2005.
Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said after the meeting with Hans Berger, head of the IGBE mining and energy union, that more talks would be held.
"The government wants a mutually acceptable agreement on coal subsidies running to 2005. The necessary decisions will be made in February 1997," Bohl said in a statement.
